To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed capacity allocation technique can be used for the optimal allocation, at runtime, of the computational resources in a shared data center, in such a way that: (i) the deadlines stated in service level agreements (SLOs) are met and (ii) the power consumption is substantially reduced.

we have developed a distributed algorithm for capacity allocation that guarantees better performance and lower energy consumption than state of the art approaches, while respecting the deadlines and avoiding penalties.

we propose a new approach for runtime capacity allocation in shared MapReduce clusters, that we model using Game Theory, that allows to achieve a substantial reduction of the energy consumption, while respecting SLAs, and that is based on a distributed algorithm that mimics MapReduce dynamics by using the interactions among the Resource Manager and Class Manager.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new techniques for runtime resource allocation in MapReduce environments, with the goal of achieving higher performance in shared clusters.
the design and implementation of a distributed algorithm for the runtime capacity allocation in a Hadoop cluster.

the development of new techniques for runtime capacity allocation in Hadoop 2.0 that can reduce the power consumption of a Hadoop cluster while guaranteeing that the deadlines stated in SLAs are respected.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work has been carried out in a very challenging and interesting context, and that we have been able to develop and validate a novel capacity allocation algorithm, which is a key element for the efficient management of Hadoop clusters.
we propose a distributed algorithm for the runtime capacity allocation in a Hadoop cluster, based on Game theory and on the MapReduce paradigm.

this paper proposes an innovative approach to runtime capacity allocation, which can be used in shared data centers to improve the overall performance of Hadoop 2.0 clusters, by means of a game-theoretic approach.

we have proposed and implemented a novel algorithm to dynamically allocate resources in a Hadooplex cluster.

the proposed approach is able to provide a better utilization of resources and a more efficient resource allocation in a MapReduce cluster.
the proposed approach can be easily applied to any MapReduce cluster, with a substantial reduction of energy consumption, and with a better management of resources.
